Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Brightlane is leaning toward Redwood for inference, but we have two non-negotiable routing requirements from our privacy/compliance group:

- All inference must execute in APAC regions (data residency).
- No automatic fallback to other regions or public/shared model variants — if APAC capacity is unavailable, requests should fail or queue, not route elsewhere.
- We also want to force usage of our dedicated quantized model (redwood-q-priv-v1) rather than any hosted variants.

Appreciate a quick read — Mara

Team — Brightlane (prospect, BL-2026-045) is asking for three things: APAC-only execution, strict no-fallback (fail/queue rather than routing out of region), and forced use of their dedicated quantized model redwood-q-priv-v1. They want these written into the contract.

2) Infra (Marcus/Dev): Operationally, what happens to latency and availability if we refuse fallback? Can we surface queueing/backpressure with clear 503/202 semantics?
3) Security (Neha): Are there any compliance blockers to pinning a customer to a dedicated quantized build? Any additional audit evidence we must produce?

Thanks — Karthik

Quick note: I support exploring this but flag two immediate concerns:
- Business risk: No-fallback increases outage risk for the customer and for our promise to keep apps live. We'll need an explicit SLA carve-out and incident runbook.
- Product scope: forcing model version per-customer is doable but we should avoid one-off code paths. Prefer policy-driven config + automation to keep maintainability.

If feasible, propose: a policy object "routing.strict_region: apac" and "routing.fallback: deny" with clear observability + opt-in in Dedicated/Private tiers only.

Laura

Subject: Re: Fwd: Brightlane routing/fallback constraints — need product/security/infra decision

Technical summary from runtime/infra side:
- Region pinning: already supported in routing layer. We can restrict request routing to APAC pools by customer ID.
- Forced model selection: we can accept a model_id override at the tenant routing layer; for dedicated/private deployments this maps cleanly. For hosted multi-tenant pools, forcing an internal quantized model (redwood-q-priv-v1) has licensing/packaging implications but is technically possible if the model is available in the APAC pool.
- No-fallback semantics: currently we have a fallback chain (APAC -> US -> EU) to reduce errors under load. To implement deny-fallback we can short-circuit the chain and return 429/503 or place requests into a customer-scoped queue. Two implementation approaches with tradeoffs:
  1) Immediate deny: return 503 with explicit error code and message. Simpler, predictable, but customer experiences request failures under overload.
  2) Customer queueing: hold requests in a tenant-scoped queue with backpressure and configurable TTL. Requires work to surface queue depth and TTL enforcement (3–4 sprints).

Operational impacts: Increased chance of visible errors; need runbook and SLA carve-out. Also need a test harness for chaos testing to ensure no global cascade.

Attachments: short design note (linked in Jira).

- Dev

Subject: Re: Brightlane - compliance and audit items for forced-region/no-fallback

Security/Compliance checklist items we will need if we agree to contract language:
- Written policy that documents no-fallback behaviour and expected error semantics (for Brightlane contract).
- Customer-specific audit logs showing region, model_id, and routing decisions for every request (retention window TBD — propose 1 year for enterprise).
- Evidence that the dedicated model build (redwood-q-priv-v1) is only present in APAC tenant pools and that key material for the model is access-controlled.
- Pen-test and SOC2 evidence: Brightlane will likely ask for a short statement that no cross-region routing occurs; prepare a signed attestation and a scoped SOC2 extract.

I can assemble the attestation doc and the log retention addendum, but we need infra to confirm the logging can be filtered by tenant and region (Marcus/Dev).

- Neha

- Forced model_id (redwood-q-priv-v1): supported for Dedicated/Private; hosted multi-tenant support possible but requires packaging/licensing confirmation.
- No-fallback: two options — immediate-deny (fast, small change) or tenant-queue (safer UX, 3–4 sprints).

4) Sales (Karthik): coordinate with Brightlane procurement on which option they want (deny vs queue) and surface pricing/SLA implications (ongoing).

I'll update Mara once we have the Product + Infra notes. If anyone is blocked, call me and I'll escalate.

Karthik
